cards.name: The Fool
cards.up: UPRIGHT: New beginning. Flowering potential. Freedom and travel. Innocence and optimism. Odd and silly behavior. Outlander. Fresh chapter.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Blindness. Ignorance. Childish. Reckless. Indiscreet. Irresponsible.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I start over?

cards.name: The Magician
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Enthusiasm. Initiative. Charisma. Flexibility. Powerful action. “As above, so below” bestows the harmony of heaven and earth. You are the universe; the universe is you. Be the magic to cast it.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Arrogance. Powerlessness. Poor communication. Hidden talents.

To right the reversal, ask:
What am I here to do?

cards.name: The High Priestess
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Stand in self-knowledge. Access inner power. Honor the sacred self. Intuition. Silence. Knowing who you are. Blueprint. Eternal. Authenticity. Mystery. Perfection. Divinity.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Prisoner of the world. Trapped and confused. Loss of faith. Out of step.

To right the reversal, ask:
What thrives inside me?

cards.name: The Empress
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Abundance. Mother. Birthing waters. Menstruation. Compassion. Creativity. Nature. Enthusiasm. Initiative. Art. Harvest. Expansion.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Suspicious behavior. Inconstant manners. Cruel thoughts. Selfish actions hide fear-based thoughts. Problematic parenting. Creative blockage.

To right the reversal, ask:
What can I nurture?

cards.name: The Emperor
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Set your sights. Embrace powerful habits. Exercise firm control. Foster leadership. Create a moveable system of rules. Harbor self-discipline. Secure the self. The present situation requires seriousness.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Father issues. Domineering impulse. Arbitrary decisions. Stubborn indecision.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I be flexible in this moment?

cards.name: The Hierophant
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Teacher and student. Mentorship working both ways. Aid and kindness. Traditions and rituals. Groups and educational settings. Teaching through actions. Lifelong learning.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Power hungry and unyielding. Shallow and deceptive. Absent and irresponsible.

To right the reversal, ask:
What lesson must I learn?

cards.name: The Lovers
cards.up: UPRIGHT: New romance. Attraction and erotic desire. Root chakra and source of life. Passionate relationship. Choice and vulnerability. Devotional energy. Life force.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Misunderstanding and contradiction. Repulsion and rejection. Ill timing. Stumbles and challenges for lovelorn couples.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I love myself?

cards.name: The Chariot
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Willpower and self-discipline. Travel and excitement. Victory, success, and achievement. Certainty in action even when the outcome is unclear. Deep, complete trust and commitment.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Slow and stifled. Listless and limp. Momentum lost and falling to the wayside. Languid pools of boredom. Offtrack.

To right the reversal, ask:
Where do I want to go?

cards.name: Strength
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Patience and gentle courage. Outwitting others. Endurance and fortitude. Using lessons of the past to forge the present self.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Weakness and cruelty. Sloppy, lazy work. Brutal acts stemming from a sense of inferiority.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I cultivate kindness to others and myself?

cards.name: The Hermit
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Introspection and solitude. Removal and sequestered isolation. Cautiousness and inward exploration. Using inner light as a beacon for others.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Exhaustion from overextending to others. Being there for everyone else but yourself. Hiding away, disguise, and escape. Avoiding what must be embraced. Stowaway.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I put myself first?

cards.name: Wheel of Fortune
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Movement. A change in luck. Going with the flow. A favorable turn of events. Cycles and universal energy.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Feeling stuck, off-balance, and out of control. Anxiety.

To right the reversal, ask:
What can I focus on to bring peace?

cards.name: Justice
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Action bears fruit. Moral issues. Sense of right and wrong. Rules. Legal issues and law-related affairs. Court proceedings and contracts. Laying down the law. Strength in responsibility and fairness. The delegation of rules.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Outlaw. Unfair. Lawless. Irresponsible. Unbalanced. Blackmail.

To right the reversal, ask:
What am I responsible for?

cards.name: The Hanged Man
cards.up: UPRIGHT: A change of perspective. Waiting. Peering deeply into the heart of mystery. Yoga and introspection. Mystics and artists. Divine mystery and profound change in which to view the world.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Amazement, motion, and second sight. Receiving an energetic transfusion. A reversed Hanged Woman card is as vibrant as it is upright.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I gaze deeper?

cards.name: Death
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Fundamental change and transformation. Root chakra. Endings and loss. Destruction and entropy. Release. The occultist’s initiation into higher levels of exploration and learning.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Unwilling to accept change. Clinging to what has vanished. Stagnation.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I let go?

cards.name: Temperance
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Complexity. Harmony. Integration. Soul alchemy. Communication. Balance. Healing. Forging. Mixing all possibility. Soul alchemy.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: One-sided conversations. Poor communication. Impatient. Careless with self and others.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I listen?

cards.name: The Devil
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Disorder of the mind. Addiction and confusion. The shadow self. The ego. The chains that enslave you. Chaos and cruelty. The overwhelming need to control a situation.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Cowering fear. Being timid when fierceness is required. Allowing others to control you.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I step into who I truly am?

cards.name: The Tower
cards.up: UPRIGHT: The field is cleared. A light bulb moment of awareness. Immediate understanding. Clash and destruction of what was never meant to be. Release of attachment. Losing what didn’t fit.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Terrified of change. Refusal to face facts. Hiding the head in the sand to avoid confrontation.

To right the reversal, ask:
What am I holding back from?

cards.name: The Star
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Inspiration. Healing. Calm after the storm. Clarity. Flow. Transcendence. Peace.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Shallow fears. Blockage. Feeling cut off. Clinging to the past to avoid moving forward.

To right the reversal, ask:
What can I accept?

cards.name: The Moon
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Sleep and dream life. Psychic nature. Subconscious becoming conscious. Emergence. Shadow becomes light.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Repressing primal urges. Uncomfortable with one’s own power and magic. Unable to integrate inner duality.

To right the reversal, ask:
What wants to emerge through me?

cards.name: The Sun
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Abundance. Love. Joy. Excellent health. Heart chakra. Expansion and exuberance. Destiny.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Sadness. Depression. Seclusion. Darkness. Dour feelings. Self-destructive behavior.

To right the reversal, ask:
What goodness can I let into my life?

cards.name: Judgement
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Ecstasy and accomplishment. Heeding the call. The message you have been waiting for. Life force. Born again but into yourself. Rising up. Alive and awake.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Refusal to listen. Nonconformity. Abandoning hopes and dreams.

To right the reversal, ask:
What helps me come alive?

cards.name: The World
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Flow. Manifestation. Travel. Glory. Culmination. Perfection. Dance. Celebration. Expression. Completion. All desires granted and wishes met. Perfect alignment.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Close to the finish line. Fear of having what you’ve always dreamed of.

To right the reversal, ask:
What helps me live in the moment?

cards.name: Ace of Wands
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Strength and power. Tremors of passion. Toe-curling desire. Virility. New options blaze to life. Miraculous spark. Beginning. Origin. Source.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Extinguished energy. The smothering of desire. Apathy and unworthiness.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I focus on the stirrings within?

cards.name: Two of Wands
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Looking ahead. Plotting and planning. Visioning. Observe the lay of the landscape to align with your desire. Bring together equal opposing forces and ideas to foster the energy of transformation.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Stunted plans. Inability to imagine the future. Exhaustion and apathy toward the situation at hand. Nothing feels worth the bother.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I take one small step?

cards.name: Three of Wands
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Magic in action. Setting your ships out to sea. Creativity and advancement. Strength in the self and knowing who you are. Believing in yourself. It is time to cast your lot and make your mark. The poetic trinity of the self, universe, and unseen mystery merge into the active magic and manifestation of personal action and intention.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Fear holds you back. Procrastination bred from unworthiness. Using your own gifts and talents against yourself.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I support my intention?

cards.name: Four of Wands
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Gatherings close to family and friends. Endless evenings, wild dancing, and delight. Sustaining the real-world results of passion projects. Stopping along the way to enjoy the journey.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Ruining a good time. Yucking another’s yum. Refusing to join in the fun. Poisonous attitude. Treachery. 

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I make space for gratitude?

cards.name: Five of Wands
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Action and sparring. Everyone fighting for themselves. Whipping people up. Combustible energy. Excitement and furor. A fun, action-packed match of wits and strength.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Drama stirred out of boredom. Amusing the self by provoking others. Unwillingness to fight.

To right the reversal, ask:
What is at stake for me?

cards.name: Six of Wands
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Victory and advancement. Blazing hearts. Inspiration. Personal ideas catch on. People wishing the best. Good graces. Bringing out the best in others. Success, with more to come.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Downplaying talent. Inability to accept compliments. Stuck in a negative spiral. Inability to experience the pleasure of the self.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I inspire myself?

cards.name: Seven of Wands
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Action and energy. Focusing on advancing the position. Personal knowledge used for empowerment. Knowledge lights the way. Advance. Risks pay off. Help arrives when least expected. Unanticipated surges of power. Let go and trust the process.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Defensive and fearful. Vicious attacks. Venom replaces pleasure. Inspiration turns to violence.

To right the reversal, ask:
Where is my advantage?

cards.name: Eight of Wands
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Everything put into the world counts. Love letters. Send messages. Call and response. Prayers in motion. Action in flight. Results are soon to be revealed.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Miscommunication. Lack of belief. Try again. Launch failure.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I approach this differently?

cards.name: Nine of Wands
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Breaking boundaries. Stepping into unknown territory. Pushing past what is possible. Formidable opponents. Strength and knowledge through embraced challenges. Experience breeds confidence.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Overwhelming obstacles. Oppression. Feeling as if the odds are stacked against oneself. Unable to navigate through current situation.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I change my course?

cards.name: Ten of Wands
cards.up: UPRIGHT: A cycle is complete. Setting out on a new path. The body regenerates. New adventure. Walking between worlds. Embracing responsibility.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Stifled. Blocked. Stuck. Uninspired.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I help those who depend on me?

cards.name: Page of Wands
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Follow passion. Trust instinct. Play with what intrigues you. Good luck abounds. Freedom surrounds you. Stoke enthusiasm. Youthful energy.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Jealousy and temper tantrums. Waste valuable energy. Break out of a rut. Explore new horizons. Is it possible to forget everything you think you know?

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I be young again?

cards.name: Knight of Wands
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Gather energy and charisma to achieve desires. Surprise yourself. Let go. Moving forward quickly. Be careful not to run out of steam. Romantic messages and passionate sentiments.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Get up and move. Exercise for the body and soul. Pent-up aggression needs to be worked out. Take a chance. Go out on a limb and challenge yourself.

To right the reversal, ask:
How far am I willing to go?

cards.name: Queen of Wands
cards.up: Charisma and charm. X factor. Dedication and passion. Renewal. Warmth inspiring others to shine. Claim your birthright.
cards.rev: Out of bounds. Rein it in. Turn attention to something useful. Discomfort stems from not being true to oneself. Follow the inner light.

cards.name: King of Wands
cards.up: Spirituality is a key factor in your situation. Adopt a lionlike attitude. Be equitable and honest in your dealings. Trust your original vision and see it through to its rightful conclusion. Great power resides within.
cards.rev: Listless. Time to begin again. The spark has extinguished.

cards.name: Ace of Cups
cards.up: UPRIGHT: An open heart with emotions flowing. Unbounded love. Beautiful beginning of affection. A fresh, artful approach to life. Splendid feelings. New opportunity in all emotional sectors. Heart opening.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Burying emotion that needs to be let out. Overly emotional for the sake of being dramatic. Valuing one’s own emotional state while disregarding the feelings of others. Cutting the self off from love.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I heal?

cards.name: Two of Cups
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Sweet romance. Amorous attraction. Pleasure and delight in another person, place, or thing. Heart’s reflection. Recognition. Intimacy. Secret marriage.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: A relationship is not as expected. Disconnection. Rejection.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I cultivate boundaries?

cards.name: Three of Cups
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Friendship, revelry, and celebration. Lifelong relationships. Gathering with those who are closest to you. Fruits of success. Divine feminine. Sharing gifts with others. Others sharing gifts with you.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Passive-aggressive behavior. Trouble within a friend group. The inability to be happy for another’s success.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I reflect the light of others?

cards.name: Four of Cups
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Emotional indulgence. Not seeing the forest for the trees. Situations changing in the blink of an eye. Staying open to the unexpected. Hidden gifts are about to be revealed. Remove personal blinders.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Emotional blockage or unexpected outpouring. Seek help, take advice, and balance emotional issues.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I look beyond the current situation?

cards.name: Five of Cups
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Disconnect. Lack of feeling. Addiction, sadness, and depression. A choice to repeat or to change the pattern. Bleak times but the freedom to move forward. What you need is right in front of you.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Old patterns are released. Avoiding emotional pitfalls. Letting go of what does not serve your highest purpose.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I fight for myself?

cards.name: Six of Cups
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Giving and receiving. Gifts from the heart. Memories, happiness, and comfort. The feeling of coming home to what you love. Connection and gratitude. Happiness and delight. Offerings of love.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Giving yourself away to those who cannot return your love and affection. Unable to accept gifts and tenderness. Replacing joy with anger and love with fury.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I practice acceptance?

cards.name: Seven of Cups
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Multiple possibilities. Choice. Options. What waits to be made manifest. Decisions. Unbound imagination. Casting effective spells manifesting with individuality and unique beauty.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Blockage preventing clarity of the big picture. Undervaluing personal gifts. Giving magic and attention away by focusing on others instead of the self.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I cultivate focus?

cards.name: Eight of Cups
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Moving on both physically and emotionally. Giving up what you have to get what you need. Departure on a grand scale on your own terms. Time to say goodbye. Taking the high road.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Stuck and stymied. Unable to release emotional bonds. Misery without cause. Wasteful excess.

To right the reversal, ask:
What should I leave behind?

cards.name: Nine of Cups
cards.up: UPRIGHT: The answer is yes. Wish fulfillment. Pleasure and happiness. Delight and alignment. Getting what you want.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Disappointment after receiving just what you asked for. The desire to turn back time. Unable to enjoy gifts. Too little, too late.

To right the reversal, ask:
What is the unforeseen consequence?

cards.name: Ten of Cups
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Celebration and delight. Home, happiness, and contentment. At home in the world. True pleasure. Deep love. Everything will be okay.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Tense home life. Family instability. The family is crowding you in. Cabin fever. Old stories and habits bring out the worst.

To right the reversal, ask:
What small adjustment brings everyone together?

cards.name: Page of Cups
cards.up: Anything is possible. Psychic and intuitive powers are in full effect. Trust what is felt. Follow your highest vibe. It is safe to explore the vastness of your imagination. Take delight in simple pleasures. Play in the world around you.
cards.rev: Stop repressing emotions. Give yourself a break. Don't take the world so seriously. Take a breath, play music, and have some fun to cultivate balance.

cards.name: Knight of Cups
cards.up: Romance and seduction using flattery and sweet nothings. Muse of art and poetry. A refusal to adapt to other's expectations. Focusing on what moves the soul. Slow, deliberate pleasure. Consider how to make your intentions known.
cards.rev: Ignoring the softer, sweeter elements of life. Rushing ahead without savoring pleasure. Lack of enjoyment due to emotional detachment.

cards.name: Queen of Cups
cards.up: An attitude of compassion, understanding, and empathy is required to move to the heart of the situation. Becoming a container for others while placing boundaries of protection around yourself. Master of your own emotional state. Reach for the sublime.
cards.rev: Off-kilter emotions. Angry outbursts, emotional meanderings, and lack of boundaries with others. Childlike tantrums and needy qualities. To be a queen, you must rein it in.

cards.name: King of Cups
cards.up: Artistic genius. Dependable and caring. Turn your attention to creative projects you can master. Celebrate all aspects of the emotional spectrum. Deep, dark waters give way to the incandescence of sunlight and pleasure.
cards.rev: Feeling sorry for yourself. Emotional immaturity. Cheating to get what you want. Hurting others out of spite. Time to grow up and take responsibility.

cards.name: Ace of Swords
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Clear thinking. Winning thoughts. Trusting what you know. Excellent plans. Sharp instincts. Triumph. Your first thought is well conveyed. Ideas come swiftly. Action is sure to follow.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Nailing down your plans. Standing strong in what you know. Refusal to budge.

To right the reversal, ask:
What is my mantra?

cards.name: Two of Swords
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Heed the inner voice. The advice of others is unneeded. Draw from experience. A choice appears that only you can make. Inner sanctum of thought. Block distraction. Step away from others. Protect the heart.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Confusion and mental turmoil. Relying too much on the advice of others. The risks arising from letting others determine what is best for you. Distraction.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I stop caring about what others think of me?

cards.name: Three of Swords
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Heartbreak, betrayal, and sadness. Heart opening. Shamanistic healing. Journey into the heart of who you are. Rewriting the story. Stay present with discomfort to move past it.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Avoiding pain that must be confronted. Old patterns have healed. Freedom from one who hurt you.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I stay present in the face of discomfort?

cards.name: Four of Swords
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Stable thoughts. Pleasure in decisions. Resting well. Assured mind, spirit, and body. A pause providing room to imagine and contemplate well into the future. A well-sent message. Restful nights. Restoration of mind, body, and soul.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: A mind in utter disarray. Not trusting what is imagined or seen in the mind’s eye.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I remove mental distractions?

cards.name: Five of Swords
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Victimhood and betrayal. An unfair fight. Mean-spirited confrontation. Delight in cruelty. Take responsibility for what is said and done. Acknowledge the role you play in relationships.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Avoiding painful situations you used to be drawn into. Refusing to partake in a crowd-sourced drama.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I speak kindly to those who intimidate me?

cards.name: Six of Swords
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Traveling with companions. Transforming the present reality. Better times lie ahead. Deep emotional bonds. Trusting instinct and insight to navigate forward, even in darkness and confusion. Knowledge that you are never alone. Forging a new path. Travel and movement.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Stuck when it is important to move forward. Consider your head and heart in equal terms.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I move ahead?

cards.name: Seven of Swords
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Getting away with it. Moving under the cover of darkness. Taking what you need. Escaping without being seen. A secret worth protecting. Willing to risk it all.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Greed and wanting everything for the self. An idea will backfire. Losing everything gained.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I reassess?

cards.name: Eight of Swords
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Shamanic initiation. Entrapment. Isolation. Violence toward the self. Struggling internally. Trying to control what cannot be tamed. Give yourself over to the challenge to conquer it.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Treachery and unforeseen circumstances. Everything thrown into disarray.

To right the reversal, ask:
How do I save myself?

cards.name: Nine of Swords
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Darkness of the mind. Paralyzing anxiety. Lost. Self-flagellating. Sleeplessness. Nightmares. Night terrors. Destructive thoughts. Anguish. Dread.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Searching for answers. Avoiding the heart of the matter. Disappointment and despair.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I shift my perspective?

cards.name: Ten of Swords
cards.up: UPRIGHT: What is done is done. Resolution of drama. Sacrifice. Important endings. Metaphorical bloodshed feeds new life. Death of the ego. The peace of finally letting go.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Wanting to free yourself but not knowing how. Confusion.
To right the reversal, ask:

How do I end this kindly?

cards.name: Page of Swords
cards.up: Innovation and intelligence. Determination stemming from an acute thoughtfulness. Laser-like attention and pushing all distractions aside. Cleverness and daring.
cards.rev: No need to look any deeper into your situation. Take what is happening at face value. Do not overthink. Be easy. Employ a light touch.

cards.name: Knight of Swords
cards.up: The ability to defend oneself articulately and intellectually. Racing ahead of others. Speedy resolution to a problem. Take action now. Go for it. What is your highest ideal? Move toward it.
cards.rev: Not thinking clearly. Moving forward without a game plan is ill-advised. Stop to consider options before making plans or communicating with others.

cards.name: Queen of Swords
cards.up: Trust how you communicate with others. Speak your mind with clarity and control. If something is required, ask for it; it shall be yours.
cards.rev: The time for demands are over. Stop talking and start observing. Speaking without thinking will only make matters worse. The situation needs time to resolve.

cards.name: King of Swords
cards.up: Deadlines are met. Bold thinking should be applied to your situation. Rules and regulations will work in your favor. Look into new and far-reaching directions. Stand in your power. Speak your mind.
cards.rev: Believe in the power of the mind. Trust your thoughts and know what you know. Listen to what others tell you. Observe carefully.

cards.name: Ace of Pentacles
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Miracles of manifestation. An opportunity comes your way. Having the resources required. Beginning a new project or new venture. Gifts are showered upon you.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Holding back when something wants to emerge. Hiding funds away for yourself at the expense of others. Not having what you need due to feelings of unworthiness.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I give?

cards.name: Two of Pentacles
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Delightful choices. Evolution and growth. Opportunities arrive. Joy in creation. Magnetic attraction based on what is put forth into the world. Duality. Enjoy the journey. Rejoice in the dance.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Keeping secrets. A refusal to let talents shine. Fear of theft.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I lighten up?

cards.name: Three of Pentacles
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Working well with others. Calling in the experts. Renovation of house and home. Building something for yourself. A project bears fruit. Craftsmanship and collaboration.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: A project comes screeching to a halt. Effort outweighing results. Power plays among collaborators.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I collaborate kindly?

cards.name: Four of Pentacles
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Desperate bid to keep what was never yours. Holding tightly to resources. Stability and growth are yours, but do not let them become a prison. Solid, self-sustaining, stable foundations.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Nothing seems to stick. House of cards that keeps blowing down. Gather your resources to make them work.

To right the reversal, ask:
What am I grasping at?

cards.name: Five of Pentacles
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Material hardship. Financial strain. Feeling left out in the cold. Isolation. Illness or physical exhaustion. Overlooking available help.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Recovery from financial loss. Seeking shelter and support. Overcoming hard times. Returning warmth.

To right the reversal, ask:
Where can I seek support?

cards.name: Six of Pentacles
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Charity and generosity. Giving or receiving help. Fair distribution of wealth. Balance of power. Gratitude. Shared success.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: One-sided generosity. Strings attached to gifts. Unbalanced power dynamics. Debt or entitlement.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I give without expectation?

cards.name: Seven of Pentacles
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Long-term results. Hard work paying off. Patience and perseverance. Pausing to assess progress. Sustainable growth.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Impatience. Disappointment with slow progress. Poor investment of effort. Lack of planning.

To right the reversal, ask:
What needs more time to grow?

cards.name: Eight of Pentacles
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Skill development. Mastery and craftsmanship. Hard work and focus. Detail-oriented effort. Taking pride in work. Dedication.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Lack of focus. Lazy efforts. Perfectionism causing delays. Uninspired routine.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I hone my skills?

cards.name: Nine of Pentacles
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Independence. Financial stability. Self-reliance. Solitary enjoyment. Luxury and comfort. Harvesting personal success.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Overreliance on others. Overspending. Feeling unaccomplished despite material success.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I honor my independence?

cards.name: Ten of Pentacles
cards.up: UPRIGHT: Family legacy. Long-term wealth and stability. Inheritance. Multi-generational support. Home and family traditions. Abundance. Deep-rooted foundation.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Family disputes over money or property. Financial instability. Breaking with traditional expectations. Loss of legacy.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I honor my roots?

cards.name: Page of Pentacles
cards.up: Look carefully into what fascinates you. Return to school or study. The answers are inside of you. Cherish those things you love with your attention. Everything is possible.
cards.rev:
Looking for something that is not there. Break attachment to what was never yours to begin with. The season is concluded. Let go. If it was meant for you, it will come back around.
To right the reversal, ask:What unseen troves of magic support me and bring focus?

cards.name: Knight of Pentacles
cards.up: Moving with mindfulness and ease. Gentle touch. The struggles you face may be self-created; therefore, the answer you require can be found within. Connect to elements of earth and animals to ground into who you are.
cards.rev:
Moving ahead without considering consequences. Caring little about others. Taking what you need without giving back.

To right the reversal, ask:How does silence protect me?

cards.name: Queen of Pentacles
cards.up: Using every talent to create a luscious lifestyle. Cooking, gardening, and decorating around the home add luxury and pleasure. Kitchen witchery and garden magic serve you well. Utilize natural energies and work in tandem with the earth.
cards.rev:
REVERSED: Being obsessive about the house and home. Creating problems where there are none. Attempting to control the natural order and flow.

To right the reversal, ask:
How can I invoke beauty?

cards.name: King of Pentacles
cards.up: Wealth and abundance. Knowing who you are. Grounded and mature. Financial growth and material stability. Having excellent business aptitude. Protecting yourself and others through wise decisions.
cards.rev:
Let go of what you think you need. Step away from food and drink; they do not hold the answers you desire but are temporary distractions. It is time to gather strength and rebuild.

To right the reversal, ask:How can I invest in my future?

decks.name: Seasons Of The Witch - Autumn Tarot
Seasons Of The Witch - Winter Tarot

cards.name: Hoodwinks
cards.up: When caught in a selfish or egotistical frame of mind, these two tricksters encourage you to pull back and try to see the non-dual aspect of reality. Maybe you've been viewing a situation or problem in your life as an either/ or choice, where there's one winner and one loser. This card invites you to shed your black-and-white thinking and remember that reality is more of a greyscale.

cards.name: Madame Pythia
cards.up: This card represents desire, temptation and attraction. Its two main readings suggest that you could either be manifesting the energy of Madame Pythia herself or that of one of her onlookers. Whatever your romantic situation, consider the positives in love that come from your attractive confidence - but also recognize the downsides that could arise from giveing into temptation completely.

cards.name: Maiden Mort
cards.up: The Maiden represents youth, vitality, sexuality and fertility. It encourages you to follow your dreams and discover new passions and interests, focus on self-discovery, seeking answers and truths. Reflect closely on any self-imposed limits and assess whether these hinder such explorations and thus stunt your growth as a person. Be true to yourself always, it is not selfish to explore and obtain your own desires and needs. But remember, throughout this journey of self-discovery, do not lose empathy.

cards.name: Kismet
cards.up: The Kismet is the carnival's very own mythical creature, similar to the Bai Ze from Chinese mythology. A symbol of fortune and good luck, the appearance of this card is overwhelmingly positive—it means that luck is on your side, and your fortunes will change for the better. So be on the lookout for opportunities that present themselves to you.

cards.name: Nuckelavee
cards.up: This card represents disease, illness and health issues. It is a sign to seek medical attention if you have perhaps been putting off doing so or merely to put one's health first and prioritize your physical well-being. It reminds us that our bodies are fragile and require essential maintenance to ensure longevity. The card represents toxicity in people and situations. Avoid these as they will poison you against others and yourself.

cards.name: Carl Scheele The Chemist
cards.up: Have you been putting off an appointment, treatment, or necessary personal discussion? Drawing this card is a directive to prioritize your own health and well-being—be it physical, mental, or spiritual. Keep in mind though, that while medicine has advanced in leaps and bounds over the past centuries, addressing one issue can cause unforeseen effects in other areas of your life. Take what the chemist prescribes, but be careful to walk the middle path between abstinence and excess.

cards.name: Molly and Wally The Twins
cards.up: Molly and Wally represent karma, especially toward the most innocent creatures humans have abused. They allow the animal spirits to sniff out and exact revenge on those who would harm or kill any vulnerable soul—whether it may be human or non-human.The twins offer justice, shelter and love for all who need it. Drawing this card is your sign to continue supporting those less fortunate than you.

cards.name: Arsenic Jane
cards.up: Arsenic Jane represents you on your journey through life. A personification of every human on our walk from childhood to death, drawing Arsenic Jane represents a fresh beginning. Your situation has been difficult recently, with the struggles you've faced having eaten away at your inner child. This card provides encouragement that if you care for your inner child, you will emerge as a stronger individual. No matter what happens at the very end of your story, you can make a positive impact around you by cultivating your sense of childlike joy.

cards.name: Sphinx
cards.up: The Sphinx is a creature from Greek mythology. Legend stated that the creature was omniscient and wise and would often befuddle men with her riddles. The appearance of this card means that the answer to a great question, mystery or the solution to a current problem or ongoing issue will reveal itself soon. This card is neutral, meaning that it does not reveal whether the answer or solution will be positive, the one the reader wants, or negative, but merely indicates an impending conclusion.

cards.name: The Puppeteer
cards.up: While puppet shows can be silly, joyful affairs, at the Carnival of Souls, this macabre puppet show invites you to look closely into the outside influences that are affecting your current situation. Are you working as the puppeteer of your own life? Or, are you being used as a puppet?

cards.name: Ludas The Wag
cards.up: This card represents generosity and kindness, giving to others, and generosity towards ourselves. Be kind to others; the karma will be returned, a reminder to pay it forward. It also represents fun and joy and the need sometimes to stop, kick off our shoes and play. It is a reminder to be silly and laugh often, whether singing our loud or dancing like no one is watching, playing a game, or being creative, have fun. Life is meaningless without pleasure. Embrace your inner child.

cards.name: Mother Mort
cards.up: In the form of the great mother, Mother Mort is a matriarch and an empress. She is a creator and a nurturer. This card represents creation in all of its forms, whether it is the creation of a business or a relationship. The keys she holds represent the germination of an idea, inspiration, and the yearning to act on such ideas. It also represents the need to be receptive to change.

cards.name: One-eyed Jack
cards.up: Have you felt out of control recently? This card represents the guiding hand of fate. While the outcome that fate has in store for you might not be what you imagine, it should be, rest assured, that what will be, will be—and prepare accordingly as best you can. Much like a riverbed guiding water on its course, you may not see the river's next turns ahead—but take comfort in knowing that a larger guiding force is about to steer your life in the right direction.

cards.name: The Amazing Miles Taddy
cards.up: The Amazing Miles Taddy is the fool at the Carnival of Souls. Like the Fool card in traditional tarot decks, he can represent both new beginnings, opportunity, and potential—as well as the downside of such lightheartedness that one might be acting recklessly and taking on too many risks.This card represents new beginnings, having faith in what is to come, improvisation, and believing that the universe has your back. Modern life involves juggling many responsibilities, which can often seem overwhelming. But remember to trust yourself, focus on your task, and not simply follow those who brag they know the way. This card is also a reminder that it is alright to take a break sometimes and not to be so harsh on ourselves when we drop the ball, so to speak.

cards.name: Dream Cadaver
cards.up: This card represents letting go of negativity; both in terms of emotions and the negative influences or people in your life. Perhaps you have a toxic friend or partner in your life, or maybe someone or something is bringing a large amount of stress, worry and negativity. Now is the time to remove them from your life. This card also represents dreams and nightmares and the importance they can often hold. Have you had a recurring dream, or have you had a particularly vivid nightmare? Think about its meaning, as it may contain essential answers and revelations.

cards.name: Fire Eater
cards.up: The Fire Eater at the Carnival of Souls, a phoenix, succumbs to flames of death, later to be reborn in a new form. Drawing this card represents both farewells and goodbyes, but also transformation and rebirth. The new beginning you have been longing for might be just around the corner. Loosen your grasp on your ego, and watch as something beautiful and new rises from the ashes.

cards.name: Professor Simberg The Artist
cards.up: Professor Simberg represents the beauty and ugliness contained within you. He only creates his masterpieces out of what he sees underneath the facade of skin. Perhaps you have been struggling with low self-confidence or body issues or with a decision to change or alter your appearance dramatically; that decision is wholly dependent on the truth behind it. It reminds us that beauty is only skin deep. The professor can see it all; his skilled hands are adept at sculpting a likeness that matches what lies beneath.

cards.name: Mirror Mary
cards.up: This card represents judgment and revelations, our true selves revealed, self-doubt, awakening, understanding and redemption vs. stagnation. It represents a period of self-growth and awareness. If you have wronged another, now is the time to make amends. If you have been wronged, the truth will be revealed, and the other party or parties will have to decide whether they do the right thing or double down. Whatever happens, remain graceful and calm, and never let them lower you to their standards. Rise above and aim to be better, knowing you can hold your head high.

cards.name: Siren
cards.up: In mythology, the Sirens are beautiful mermaids who lure sailors towards their death with alluring songs. Much like the shifting ocean, this card contains different moods, and drawing it comes with two main interpretations. In the first, your life situation mirrors that of the sailors: Is there something that has been tempting you? If so, it needs reevaluation. In the second interpretation, you could be the siren herself, trapped and hungry with a secret power that you're nearly ready to spring upon the unsuspecting antagonist in your life.

cards.name: Crone Mort
cards.up: The Crone Mort is a symbol of transformation and rebirth. She represents the end of one cycle and the beginning of another. She is the one who can help you let go of the past and embrace the future. She is the one who can help you find your way through the darkness and into the light. She is the one who can help you find your way home.

cards.name: The Momento Mori Machine
cards.up: This card represents the fleeting nature of time. It may be a sign that you should dedicate time to something you have always wanted to do or a reminder that time is running out on an important decision. Either way, be cognisant that time is short and that unnecessary delays or indecisiveness can lead to you missing out on something positive. This card is a reminder to live life in the moment, forget the past, and look ahead to the future.

cards.name: Bone Fairy
cards.up: This card represents a hunger for something new or a new adventure coming into your life. Book that holiday, ask for that promotion, and ask that person you find attractive for a date. This card is a sign tto spread your wings, fly, and seek new adventures. It can also represent a cage you wish to escape, such as a bad relationship or a job you hate. Take the plunge and seek something better.

cards.name: Morrigan The Great Queen
cards.up: Drawing this card represents upcoming strength when you're in the spotlight, in a moment of conflict, or in an important discussion. The Great Queen rides alongside you—so have courage in yourself, and trust that fate is on your side. Just don't get too attached to any one particular outcome, as Morrigan might know more than you about how the situation will resolve itself.

cards.name: King Of Crows
cards.up: This card represents the need to keep your guard against someone or something. Now is the time to protect yourself and your loved ones from potential dangers on the horizon. You might sense threats approaching—this card signals that you should trust that intuition, preparing to take on the role of protector. Set clear boundaries and exercise caution.

cards.name: Witch In The Well
cards.up: The Witch in the Well does not take sides in disputes, battles, or personal conflicts. She sees the truth and reveals it in what can be the harshest voice in the universe. Have you been keeping secrets recently? Is there something you're hiding from others, or hiding from yourself? This card suggests that these lingering secrets will rise to the surface soon.

cards.name: The Amazing Sluagh
cards.up: Prepare yourself and keep a watchful eye in all your dealings. This card reminds you to remain cautious and prepare for you future security—you never know what unexpected event might drop out of the sky to shock you. Alternatively, if you've been going through a rough situation recently, drawing this card signals that help might arrive in the near future from an unexpected source.

cards.name: The Astounding Lady Makhaira
cards.up: Often, things do not go our way, which can be difficult for us to accept, but our refusal to do so can hinder our personal growth. This card means accepting something you have been struggling with, even if it is unpleasant (hard to swallow). Doing so allows you to move on emotionally and find happiness and peace beyond the immediate.The sword swallower is also a communicator, able to twist and bend into seemingly impossible shapes and positions. If you have been bending over backward to accommodate others at the expense of yourself, this is your sign to stop. Your health and happiness are just as important as that of others, and it is ok to prioritize your own physical and mental well-being. If the things you are doing go unappreciated, then stop doing them.

cards.name: Worm Tongue
cards.up: This card serves as motivation to be honest with yourself and others. If you come into conflict soon, ask yourself, "Is my ego getting in the way of honesty? Is this conflict truly worth the repercussions of a fight?" Right the wrongs that a lie has sown. If not, the harvest will never yield good fruits.

cards.name: The Ngenechen
cards.up: The Ngenechen is a governing creature—a supreme being that oversees nature, humans, and the community of beings on earth. However, the fact that this statue in its booth at the carnival is moth-covered and dusty hints that something is amiss, that you have not taken the time recently to connect with and honor the earth and its life force. Getting caught up in the web of everyday struggles and situations is easy. How can you reconnect with nature and your ancestors?

cards.name: Sandman
cards.up: Have you been burnt out from work and life recently? Sleep deprived and feeling drained? This card represents the need for you to rest, slow down and recharge. Fatigue from work, stress and relationships are affecting your internal harmony. It's vital that you clear the sand from your eyes and regain your focus and love of life—or else the Sandman might visit you in a negative mood, which will just make your situation worse.

cards.name: Lightbringer
cards.up: The Light Bringer provides illumination for the carnival goers, guiding them along their journeys among the booths and tents. Much like fire itself, a light bringer is neutral to human endeavors—it can provide warmth and comfort, provide destruction, or provide cleansing, rebirth, and the opportunity to rebuild.The Light Bringer represents illumination, energy and epiphany. Like fire, this light can take many forms, shifting from positive to negative or somewhere in between. Are you in a situation where you feel doubt about your past choices? The Light Bringer card reveals that you you are on the correct path and should continue trusting the course you've laid for yourself.

cards.name: Fehu
cards.up:
The skills and gifts you have within you are your greatest treasure. They will never be stolen. Pay attention to the way you view the links between personal power and wealth. Prosperity needs to be developed over time – and then shared.  


I am the way to wealth,
The power of having and moving,
The freedom of having enough,
With more to come.
I carry my treasure.
Within me is all.
I am Fehu.
Fehu (pronounced, “fay-who”) is one of the runes of the Elder Futark. It literally means “cattle”, and the symbol itself resembles...
The Vikings, who travelled quite a bit, had to carry portable forms of wealth with them as they traded or explored. Their wealth, therefore, wasn't measured just in gold. Cattle and other livestock, for instance, represented a type of mobile wealth – wealth that was literally “on the hoof”, so this rune is an apt symbol for the idea of prosperity within the Viking paradigm.  


The Vikings also relied upon the development of a variety skills. Boat builders, carpenters, stone masons, weapon makers, hunters, weavers, storytellers, artists – whatever your skill, when you developed it with excellence, it was seen as a valuable treasure. You could take this portable form of prosperity with you wherever you went, and your craft, unlike gold or jewels, could never be stolen.

cards.name: Uruz
cards.up:
Build personal power ethically, from the inside out. Endurance and resilience are important now. Our will can change our fate – it can forge a path where there is none. Look to your health and vitality, for these may need healing.
I am the flowing force of life,
The focus, the blood pulsing,
The oats being sown,
The uncontrolled wildness,
Tenacious and not quite polished.
I am Uruz.
Uruz (pronounced, “uh-rooze”) is a rune of the Elder Futark that represents physical, mental and spiritual power and the concept of will.
Building personal power is only valuable if we do so from the inside out. If we reply upon external validation, we will always be in a weak position, for we cannot control others. Developing self-trust, self-esteem, self-care and self-knowledge will go a long way to securing a strong, grounded and authentic sense of self that can withstand the battering life can bring.
Many of us surrender our will or our real selves due to early childhood trauma or a need to fit in. Uruz reminds us that not only does our true self never go away it is always far superior to any mask that we may have had to – or chosen to – wear. No matter what has happened to us, with the help of divine energies, we can rebuild our personal power and will ourselves back to wholeness.
I have this rune embroidered on the backpack I wear when I attempt difficult physical endeavours like mountaineering. It reminds me that I can do what I have set out to do, that resilience is something grown and learnt. Uruz shows me that it is the journey that is the joy, not just the destination.

cards.name: Thurisaz
cards.up:
Do not get drawn into unnecessary drama. There are many sides to every story, so make sure you research a situation thoroughly before making a decision. Ignorance is no excuse. Choose wisdom and remove the old thorn in your side. Choose the positive flow of enthusiasm, fecundity and passion, rather than aggression, small-mindedness and force.  


I am the hammer of wisdom:
I smash ignorance,
Exploding smallness,
Expanding outwards,
The thorn no longer in my side.
I am Thurisaz.
Thurisaz (pronounced, “thoor-ee-saws”) is part of the Elder Futark. Although often referred to as a “thorn”, this rune more accurately represents Thor’s hammer, Mjöllnir, and the god himself. Thor, a protective figure, who defended Asgard from the giants, is the hero one calls upon to fight for freedoms and balanced expansion.
The hammer can easily be misconstrued as a dull brute of a weapon, but in this case the hammer is used to smash ignorance and small mindedness, as well as clear away untruth. There is a solidity that Thurisaz requires, an acknowledgement that we have the wisdom and tools we need within us – that we do not always have to look outward for validity.  


Thurisaz suggests that courage may be needed to overcome our hesitancy to strive for greater creativity or prosperity. Both self-sabotage and chronic procrastination are challenges for many. Thurisaz gives us the confidence to break through these forms of fear with passion and gladness.

cards.name: Ansuz
cards.up:
Improved communication, clear thinking and wise action are all of great importance, now. Do not deny what someone or something really is in favour of a kinder perspective. Find order in chaos. We have inherited both positive and negative aspects from our ancestors, and it is useful to know both. The universe is conspiring to open up new ways for you.
I inhale.
I am filled with your divinity,
The spark of all that is.
Awareness floods ignorance.
My blood sings in recognition.
I exhale
The chaos and stagnancy.
I am Ansuz.
The great Allfather Odin breathed life and inspiration into each and every human. The Norse believed that our intellect and life began in the very first inhalation after birth and ended with the final exhale at death. So every breath was a gift from the gods and the universe itself. The nature of this gift of air was Ansuz.
Ansuz, (pronounced, “awn-sooze”) a rune from the Elder Futark, concerns itself with all aspects of communication – from listening to thought to speech. But its key relates to the energy behind that communication. Ansuz asks that we communicate with clarity, honesty, accuracy and with some order. The Norse understood that the world was chaotic and dynamic, but to name things, to describe them well, gave the world some order and stability, which was useful at all levels of experience.
Listening to our own intuition and the messages of the higher powers, including ancestor and divine energies, is also part of the message, here. We have inherited the blood of countless ancestors, known and unknown, and with it their life force and physicality. It is not enough to believe that we have the blue eyes of our grandmother or the hands of our great-grandfather. It is also important to understand that we have the bravery of the first and the ability to build of the second. Yet, too, we may have inherited negative aspects of a forebear, and we must name these, as well, to bring balance to our lives.

cards.name: Raidho
cards.up:
Your joys are signposts to your purpose and destiny. The journey is as important as the destination. Focus on the now, rather than the burdens of the past or the unrealised future. Stretch. Aim for new horizons. Work with the rhythms of life, not against them.
As the wheel turns,
I am at the centre, seeing all things
As they are, right now;
Being within each step.
Free to choose,
Blue sky, green fields.
I am Raidho.
With lives deeply connected to the seasons, the Norse were more mindful of the “now” of life as it rhythmically unfolded than are we. They ate, lived, travelled and even raided according to the seasons. Raidho (pronounced, “ride-ho”), a rune that is part of the Elder Futark, reminds us to focus on every aspect of the now. Doing so will make each day rich and full of wisdom and awareness.  


The Vikings were adventurers and pioneers. They travelled great distances, and understood that their journeys were to be as treasured as their destinations. In keeping with this concept, Raidho asks us to focus on every precious step of our own personal journeys and not to concern ourselves too much with what might happen in the future or what has happened in the past. In fact, Raidho suggests we unburden ourselves of the weight of the past entirely and step into the new unencumbered, so as to make the journey both easier and more joyful.  


By asking us to ride the natural flow, Raidho offers an energy of personal freedom. If we reject others’ time frames for us, their unreasonable expectations and their opinions and, instead, look to our own sense of timing and our own feeling of the rightness of that to which we are drawn, we will experience the space and freedom to choose wisely and without excessive anxiety.

cards.name: Kenaz
cards.up:
The way forward is illuminated. Be the change you wish to see. Don't just talk – embody your message to the world. No one can know everything, so learn from trusted others or elders. By illuminating our shadows, we understand ourselves and our behaviours more deeply.
The way the craftsman  


Runs his hands over the wood and knows  


What is already within it,  


As the creation floats to the surface,  


Lit from within...  


The knowledge of both appears,  


Obvious for those that would see.  


I am Kenaz.  


In the days of the Vikings, there were no formal schools, and the ability to read and write was rare. Therefore, skills were passed from one person to another by example, over an extended period of time, much like today's trade apprenticeships. If you were a boat builder, for instance, you taught others boat building, step by step. If you were a blacksmith, those who wanted to learn from you would start by watching you, then move on to building and stoking the fire, then to finding the metal and, finally, by practicing transforming the metal into things of beauty and use.  


The teacher engaged not only to show the student the processes of their craft, but also to reveal the strengths and weaknesses in the student's “way”, and this, it was believed, increased the student's artistry and craft. This kind of magic – the alchemy among the teacher, the student and that which was being created – is the illumination at the heart of Kenaz.  


Kenaz (pronounced, “kane-awze”) is both the torch and the fire of kinship (“ken-ship”). It is the force that shows us the right way forward for us and reveals to us the knowledge we need to be at our best. The Vikings would often turn to elders or others who had experience in a process or subject and seek their co-operation. Then those with the knowledge would share it in formal counsels convened to solve whatever issue was at hand.

cards.name: Gebo
cards.up:
Seek equality in your relationships, especially intimate relationships. Avoid people pleasing and co-dependence. Family and work harmony is paramount. You will be acknowledged for your fine work and your good deeds. A gift will be matched. There is natural justice that runs through life – this will be upheld.  


We agree to union,  


One that is sacred and equal,  


Side by side.  


A gift is given,  


Circles back in kind.
Harmony is won,
Justice is invited.
I am Gebo.
According to Viking lore, marriages and other unions were created under vows made to the gods. The meeting of souls in these sacred unions was not taken lightly. There were expectations on both sides. Harmony in marriage, equality in provisionary duties and parity in kinship roles all were valued by the Norse peoples. Even the gods were called upon to provide guidance and protection in return for the worship, sacrifice and honour they received.
While as modern people, we may not relate completely to the ethical standards of the Vikings, we must understand that, in lieu of sophisticated court systems, they held to a process of justice and judgment that was weighted on the severity of the transgression. Gebo (pronounced, "gay-boo") reflects this balance. What was "given" to someone, be it positive or negative, was expected to be returned. So, if a host received their guest with hospitality, providing them with food, drink, shelter and safety, all this was given with the expectation that the host would receive equal hospitality one day. Or, at the very least, that their guest would respond by being trustworthy. On the other hand, if someone acted with cunning and trickery or destroyed another's property, this too would be repaid in kind.
Gebo also asks us to heed the laws of nature and find harmony with them. If we humans work as a part of nature not apart from nature, there are countless benefits to be had, not the least being improvements in our own mental and physical health and the sustainability of our planetary resources.

cards.name: Wunjo
cards.up:
Seek joy actively – it is the most important aspect of your life right now. Loyalty in tough times. Working for and with the community is a positive move. Long-held wishes can come true, now, when you accept support and input from others.
The bell of the new rings out,
Ringing in my happiness,
Calling in the balance,
Signalling my friends,
Singing in the halls,
I am grateful.
I am Wunjo.
Wunjo (pronounced, "won-joe" or "won-yo") is one of the runes of the Elder Futhark and primarily held messages of joy and of positive connection with the community and the gods. Wunjo declared the importance of establishing harmony and alliances between individuals, groups and the wider community. This emphasis reflects the Vikings' great appreciation for the power of achievement possible when common, not just individual, focus was applied.
Viking life was a busy one. The people, who lived in a harsh, northern environment, had to work hard just to sustain life. Their communities were often either preparing for or recovering from raiding. But even though their labour may have seemed all-consuming, they always made time for ritual, music, dancing and other activities that invoked joy. In fact, evoking joy was seen as one way to knit together disparate groups.
Wunjo reminds us to always make a place for joy in our lives and look for a more light-hearted approach when we can. The moments we can label happy or joyful should be cherished and remembered. While happiness was understood as cyclic – no one could be happy all the time – the qualities of pleasure and happiness were treasured and sung about.

cards.name: Hagalaz
cards.up:
You are coming to a period of restriction – be wary not to extend your energies too much. Current difficulties may require major change, but this too will pass. Hardship can be endured. Resilience is necessary. You can learn from the current situation. You are being distracted by drama.
The sting
Of hardship;
The venom, the famine
Of what you expect or don't want;
The hope destroyer,
The wrecker of crops,
The plague:
But this too shall pass.
Hagalaz (pronounced, "ha-ga-larz") is a rune of the Elder Futhark and literally means "hailstones". In the north, hailstones could wreck homes and crops and so were seen as a symbol of destruction and hardship. Hagalaz is the herald of old patterns returning, of things that have not been dealt with raising their destructiveness once again. Happily, it also signals that, once dealt with, even the most difficult situation can pass, leaving us with lessons learned and the resilience to come back stronger than ever before.
Hagalaz is the ninth rune, and nine – a number that was mentioned all through the Eddas – was a magical number of great potent in the Norse cosmos. Great change, it was said, can happen after nine days. As a protective number, and one that completes change, Hagalaz may be asking us to hold our ground, to take shelter and wait until things get better.

cards.name: Nauthiz
cards.up:
Break free of obsessions. A new love will come into your life. You need less than you think. Be wise about separating needs from wants. Moderation is the key.
Love,
But not too much.
Burn,
But do not burn yourself.
Attract,
But not so you cannot be free.
Desire,
But without obsession.
I am Nauthiz.
Nauthiz (pronounced, "now-this") is one of the runes of the Elder Futhark. Nauthiz concerns itself with the nature of desire and explores need. The design of the rune resembles two sticks being rubbed together to cause fire, and the word can mean "need-fire".
Nauthiz warned about obsessions around needs and desires – particularly in regards to love and possessions. The Norse saw the potential for greed in both areas. While we need both love and a certain number of possessions, we must be discerning and ask ourselves what is necessary and what is excess. Another question to consider is this: What does an insatiable drive for riches or a bottomless hunger for love actually cost?
Because of its association with love, Nauthiz is also commonly used in love magic. Women were said to draw the rune on the back of a piece of jewellery or hide it in their clothing to attract a particular lover. As a rune governed by fire, Nauthiz was said to increase passion or, alternatively, to temper it.

cards.name: Isa
cards.up:
A temporary pause or halt. It is prudent to stop and wait for a better time. Be silent and regroup. Understand that something may be frozen in place for a time – this is beneficial. Do not allow others to control you or your time.
What flows may be stilled
For a time.
What sings may be silenced
For a time.
But its nature is movement,
And it will return
Paused, quiet,
To what it is.
I am Isa.
The Vikings were surrounded by ice: Glaciers, icy mountains, frozen rivers and streams, all were commonplace to their environment much of the year. The way that the normally flowing element of water was stilled into ice was magical to the Norse, and this "pausing" of things is what Isa represents.
Isa (pronounced, "ees-a") means "ice" and is one of the Elder Futhark. If we consider the impact of ice on water, we can see that it exerts a steadying control. It slows the water's path; it makes it "wait". For us, Isa can be used to quiet an unsteady mind or a racing heart. It is an excellent aid to meditation and a focus for times when we need to slow down our decision-making.
Isa also focuses the will, that steely, somewhat icy part of ourselves that may need to be activated to accomplish something difficult. It helps us draw upon our reserves and settles our flightiness.

cards.name: Jera
cards.up:
Harvest the fruits of your hard work. What you reap is what you sow. Creating connection and harmony with the land is beneficial for you. Calm and nourish yourself through contact with nature. Change will happen gradually, not overnight.
A seed is planted,
A miracle of possibility,
And it grows
Strong, made of sunlight
And water and work;
A living treasure
To hold, to harvest;
Reward for right action.
I am Jera.
The primary message of Jera (pronounced, "yehr-ah") has to do with the various harvests in our lives. As a people who collected seeds from which to grow crops, who bred and raised animals, who cut and cured the lumber from which they built their powerful boats, the Vikings understood both the necessity of hard work and the cycles of development and growth that culminated in the harvest of the fruit of that work. They also understood that to grow in a skill took time and dedication and could not be hurried.
The Vikings also recognised and valued the ideal of ethical action. They saw right action as deserving of reward – not according to karma, but simply in terms of reaping what we have sown. Like the rune Gebo, Jera deals in the idea that what is given – or, in this case, planted – is what will be harvested. In this way, Jera looks to the future. It highlights the concept that our actions today, and every day, count.

cards.name: Eihwaz
cards.up:
Do not be afraid of death – it is just another part of life. You will experience a new beginning once you have completed the current cycle, but not before. Set your boundaries clearly, and you will be protected.
I scrape the sky,
Tall and straight.
My roots deep in the underworld,
Begin again,
When all is dead.
Gone is what was;
I rejoice in what is.
I am the centre.
I am Eihwaz.
Eihwaz (pronounced, "ay-was" or yew-was) is associated with the yew, a tree sacred to the Norse. The yew is tall and very vertical, and if we consider the position of Eihwaz within the sequence of the twenty-four runes, we see it occupies the middle point, its upright shape signalling the centre. Eihwaz is also a rune of protection and relates in this way to the yew, as well, which is both protective and dangerous. The needles of the yew tree are poisonous, and it is this poison that protects the tree from predators.
Death in the Viking cosmos was not seen as something to fear, particularly if one was brave and ethical in life. The Vikings' beliefs did not promise rebirth, specifically, but they did promise those who were chosen an afterlife spent with the gods and goddesses, feasting and fighting in their halls.
In keeping with the courage of the Vikings in the face of death, Eihwaz, which is mainly concerned with the power of endings as well as beginnings, removes the fear of both figurative and literal death, while inviting spiritual confidence. If we are frightened to let something go, Eihwaz is helpful to us. If we need to let an old habit die or are afraid to cut something back or fear that something may never start anew after that "death", this rune gives us the confidence to allow the "good death" to occur.

cards.name: Perthro
cards.up:
Search your memory for the answer. You have had experience with this issue before. You will be coming into a period of good luck. Ready yourself to receive luck by preparing a base of hard work. There is more than one way to solve the current problem.
The dice fall
Where they may,
But all is not purely fate.
Will is strong,
And flows through the tree,
And changes the carvings, too.
Great things can happen
When all combine.
I am Perthro.
The Norse were very fond of betting games, including tossing dice or stones from a cup. This was both a simple entertainment as well as a way for men to pass the time between battles. Perthro, (pronounced, "pear-throw") which is in the shape of a dice cup, considers the questions about what is down to luck and what is based on will. When dice are thrown, while we think that the outcome is just chance, how we shake the cup and the angle and strength of the toss all influence the roll of the dice. Looked at this way, can we really say the roll is pure chance?
Perthro is said to be ruled by the Norns, the female deities that carve the fate of all in the bark of Yggdrasil and feed the tree with the flowing Waters of Wyrd (destiny). It is fitting, then, that this rune reminds us that nothing is set in stone (or carved in wood, in this case), and that we all experience a mixture of fate, luck and free will.
While some people may choose to sit back, let things take their course and accept that they will get what they get, others choose to influence their future. These people base their choices on their awareness of the gifts fate has given them – and understand that the more you know, the more you know how to achieve your desires. As we consider how to shape our lives, we can choose to push against fate or move with it.

cards.name: Elhaz
cards.up:
Be courageous. Fear is a necessary part of courage. Differentiate between what is yours and what belongs to others. Respect others' property and boundaries. Step forward and do what is right, even if others do not. Develop deeper connections with the plants and animals who share this planet.
I stomp the ground,
And my breath is like smoke.
My head is steady,
The points of bone turned outwards.
My family is behind me,
Ancestors all.
I can hear their breath, the beat of their heart
Behind me,
And I step through my fear.
I am Elhaz.
Elhaz (pronounced, "el-haz") literally means "elk", and is one of the Vikings' most powerfully protective runes. It resembles the antlers of a stag, which provide protection and show strength. Protective talismans almost always featured Elhaz, and it was intoned (sung) as a protection before undertaking dangerous activities.
Elhaz asks us to be courageous and to examine the role of fear within that context. If we act when we are genuinely unafraid, can we actually be considered courageous? Or does courage mean that we take action when we feel fear? Overcoming such fears is at the heart of this rune. With its encouragement, we trust that we will be protected by something higher than ourselves. We have faith. We may feel fear, but we bravely do what we believe to be right, anyway.
Where Thurisaz is sacred to the god Thor, and Perthro to the Norns, Elhaz is ruled by the mighty Valkyries, who rewarded those who fought bravely in battle and died. The Valkyries chose the best and bravest of those who perished on the fields of battle and took them to either Odin or Freyja to live within their halls. The most fervent wish of Viking warriors was to spend the afterlife celebrating with fine companions and fighting alongside Odin in Valhalla or Freyja in Fólkvangr.
Elhaz was commonly painted on shields and engraved on battle weapons. Even in modern Scandinavian countries, Elhaz is often painted on gates and fences to protect householders and their property from harm.

cards.name: Sowulo
cards.up:
You are on purpose; you are on the right path. You may need to leave others behind to reach your goal. Truth is right in front of you, should you choose to see it. You may have experienced dark times, but your future is bright.
I turn my face towards the sun,
And the path stretches out
in front of me.
I know
I have learnt the truth.
It is a solitary thing,
But brightly it shines.
Right action it is.
I am Sowulo.
Sowulo (pronounced, "so-iōlo") is the rune of the sun, Sol. As the sun illuminates all, Sowulo concerns itself with revealing the truth: truth regarding personal purpose and intent, truth within one's self and truth in the dissemination of information and in speech.
In the absence of written contracts, the Vikings' word was their truth and their bond. Truth is one of the nine virtues mentioned in the Eddas, where people are warned about setting and breaking false troths. To the ancient Norse, the word had real currency and worth. Being truthful (or not) could be the difference between surviving (or not).
This rune asks us to consider whether or not we are being true to ourselves – whether or not we are following our true path. Are we living according to the standards of others, rather than our own? Does our work take full advantage of our inherent gifts? Or are we hiding our light under a basket? Have we put on a mask to hide our truest self, lest it be seen or damaged further? How closely are we living in accordance with who we are?

cards.name: Teiwaz
cards.up:
Have faith. All your hard work and sacrifice will pay off. Self-sacrifice is necessary to achieve your goals. You will have success in legal matters. Create something new, and it will grow into something powerful. Focus your will strongly and with clarity.
I step forward,
Knowing that it is
Not all about what is for me,
But what is right
For all.
My will I focus.
What is new will flourish.
My actions are louder than words.
I am Teiwaz.
Teiwaz (pronounced, "tyr-was") is ruled by the god Tyr, who sacrificed his hand to Fenrir the wolf for the good of his community. It is told that the Aesir (the gods of Asgard), afraid that Fenrir would destroy them, decided to bind the great wolf, but had to trick him to do so. They asked Fenrir to use his great strength to test some bonds for them, assuring him they would let him go if he were unable to break them on his own. Fenrir was rightly suspicious. He asked, for insurance, that one of the gods place his hand in Fenrir's mouth and said that if the gods did not release him, that hand would be Fenrir's.
Tyr, who knew the truth of the trap, also knew the cost of not binding the wolf for his community. The only god to offer himself for this challenge, he was bound to Fenrir and ultimately lost his hand at what became known as the "wolf joint", the wrist.
Community and family were of the utmost importance to the Vikings, and sacrifice of self for the greater good was highly honoured. For example, warriors, who risked their lives for the community, were rewarded, even after death, by the gods. Even such mundane self-sacrifice as holding back seeds for the next planting season, rather than consuming them all, was in alignment with Teiwaz – as was refraining from butchering breeding stock, even if meant your family went hungry for a time. For us modern folk, the energy of Teiwaz may be expressed in the act of saving for a home or for our children's education, rather than buying luxuries.
Teiwaz concerns positive self-sacrifice, legal matters and agreements. It asks us to hold to our agreements, even those we make with ourselves. For instance, if we decide to bring our body into balance, but eat unhealthy food, we are breaking Teiwaz. However, if we are honourable with ourselves and our word, we will be rewarded with what we seek.

cards.name: Berkano
cards.up:
From something small and insignificant, something big will grow. A birth (literal or figurative) will change your life. Take the current opportunity for a fresh start. Keep your plans close to your chest. Silence is wisdom's best reply.
A tiny seed,
Fruit of mine own,
Sets down upon the softness,
Its roots small but determined.
No one sees, no one hears,
And all grows stronger;
Ready soon, but not yet.
My will made physical,
I am Berkano.
Berkano (ber-karn-oo) is the rune of the birch, a straight, beautiful white-barked tree with eye-like markings on its trunk. Birches are the Norse tree of new beginnings, and Berkano has, at its energetic heart, two concepts: birth and secrecy.
For Viking women, giving birth was dangerous. When a woman went into labour, she was taken to a women-only sanctuary, away from men and children. There, the other women sang songs of welcome and magic to ease the mother's pain. If the birth was successful, the doors were opened to all the members of the family and new stories and magic were woven to integrate the child into his or her family and the wider community.
Berkano was also used to mark vows of silence or of secrecy, and those that broke such oaths were punished. Today, with gossip extending into bullying and other negative business, the balancing energies of Berkano are needed more than ever.
When we are birthing something new, whether it be a new business, a creative project or a new relationship, it is wise to keep our plans and dreams quiet and protected. Why? Because our plans are the most vulnerable at the early stages of growth. Just like a foetus in the womb, the early days are the most risky. Therefore, it is wise to keep that which is new and precious close to our chests while it gains power and momentum. Many a project or dream is crushed in its early stages by someone's careless critique or negative comment.

cards.name: Ehwaz
cards.up:
Take speedy action. Open yourself to the power of flow. It benefits us to work with the rhythms of the natural world. Equine-assisted therapy may be of comfort to you. Eat seasonally available foods and notice the particular energies of each season. We are not our past.
The wind, it works its way
Through my hair, a crown of ink.
I smell its direction.
I feel its sway.
My legs, they hold
To the warmth of fur,
The bellows of breathing.
Together,
Forward,
Now.
I am Ehwaz.
Ehwaz (pronounced, "ay-waz"), is the rune of the horse, and it tells us of the importance of flow, rhythm and the gaining of momentum over time. Good riders adapt their bodies and minds to the rhythm of each of their horse's gaits: walk, trot, canter and gallop (or, in the case of Icelandic horses, their special gliding "tolt"). In doing so, they become one with their steed, bringing grace, ease and a deep connection between human and horse.
Ehwaz suggests we bring this same sensitivity to our everyday lives. That, rather than resisting the flow, we adapt to – even enjoy – the rhythm of life as we move with it. There is huge power in riding with the energy, not against it. For example, we can align with the changing seasons, withdrawing with the introverted nature of winter, and setting forth new plans in the fertile spring. Even the foods available differ from season to season, and scientists agree that eating seasonally is better for the health of our bodies.
Ehwaz is also a rune of the now, not the past nor the future. It reminds us that by being where we are and enjoying the fullness and completeness of this present moment we create a more mindful and enjoyable future.

cards.name: Mannaz
cards.up:
Develop yourself in all the ways you can. Fulfil your potential. Do not shy away from the collective consciousness. Human nature means mistakes are made – but we can learn from them. Working with and for the community is becoming important for you. Be rational about an issue, rather than emotional.
From the gods' breath
I came and was made whole:
Life given,
Fates chosen,
Wyrd bestowed and flowed.
But it is up to me now
To move and to choose.
It is up to me to shimmer the carvings,
To shake the tree.
I am Mannaz.
If Ehwaz represents the horse, Mannaz (pronounced, "man-awze") represents us: humans, humanity, humankind. Our common strengths and weaknesses remind us that we are all human, that we are more alike than we are different.
The Vikings relied on all the members of their communities to contribute to the collective wellbeing – as well as fulfilling their personal fate and spiritual energy. To the Vikings, this combination – the personal striving for excellence in a chosen field and the responsiveness to the needs of the community as a whole – was the recipe for a successful society. The rune Mannaz asks for both unapologetically.
This rune also indicates a need for a stronger connection between the gods and man, for greater trust in the divine.
